extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers/graduate students/developers working with graded modules and resolutions), i.e., people using the gradedModules.lib library
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in the gradedModules.lib SINGULAR library (procedures to build and manipulate graded objects, compute syzygies/resolutions, produce random graded maps, and lift maps between resolutions). Each entry gives usage, return value, purpose, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: KeneshlouMatrixPresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: KeneshlouMatrixPresentation(intvec a), intvec a. Return: graded object. Purpose: matrix presentation for direct sum of omega^a[i](i) in form of a graded object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage examples provided: LIB "gradedModules.lib"; ring r = 32003,(x(0..4)),dp; def N1 = KeneshlouMatrixPresentation(intvec(2,0,0,0,0)); grview(N1); -> shows graded homomorphism output. Example outputs demonstrate the graded homomorphism shape (e.g., r^2 <- 0, r(-1)^3 <- 0, r^2 + r(-1)^3 <- 0). The procedure returns a graded object representing a matrix presentation; examples show grview(...) for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: grsyz
rubrics_metrics.description: grsyz(M), graded object M. Return: graded object. Purpose: compute graded syzygy of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: construct module A, call grview(A) then grview(grsyz(A)); the output is a graded homomorphism describing the syzygy module (matrix form with degrees). Examples include using grgroebner and then grview(grsyz(...)) and printing the resulting matrix; demonstrates expected zero syzygy cases as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: grres
rubrics_metrics.description: grres(M, l[, b]), graded object M, int l, int b. Return: graded resolution = list of graded objects. Purpose: compute graded resolution of M (of length l) and minimise it if b was given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive examples: constructing module A, computing grgroebner(A), and calling grres(B, 0) to produce and grview a graded resolution. Example output shows a graded resolution printed as a chain of graded homomorphisms (e.g., R <-- d_1 --, R(-4)^2 + ... <-- d_2 --, etc.) and verifies D^2==0 by computing grprod(C[i], C[i+1]). The documentation shows how to inspect degrees and map matrices with grview, and how to use the returned list to traverse maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: grlift
rubrics_metrics.description: grlift(M, N), graded objects M and N. Return: transformation matrix (graded object???). Purpose: compute graded matrix which the generators of submodule Im(N) in terms of Im(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: build modules P and D, then def G=grlift(D,P); grview(G); output shows 'Graded homomorphism: r(-1) + r(-2) <- r(-2), given by a matrix, with degrees...' The documentation demonstrates verifying ASSUME(0, grisequal( grprod(D, G), P) ); i.e., grlift produces a matrix G s.t. composition expresses generators of one image in terms of the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: grprod
rubrics_metrics.description: grprod(M, N), graded objects M and N. Return: graded object. Purpose: compute graded product M * N (as composition of maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: form modules A and B (e.g., B = grsyz(A)), then D = grprod(A, B); grview(D); expected result is a (zero) matrix when B is a syzygy (printed output shows zero rows/columns). The docs note that grprod is used to check properties like syzygy composition = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: grgroebner
rubrics_metrics.description: grgroebner(M), graded object M. Return: graded object. Purpose: compute graded groebner basis of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: module A defined, then module B = grgroebner(A); grview(B); shows how grgroebner returns a graded homomorphism (a processed/grobnerized form) suitable for further resolution computations. Example demonstrates that grgroebner preserves graded structure in the output.

rubrics_metrics.name: grconcat
rubrics_metrics.description: grconcat(A, B), graded objects A and B, dst(A) == dst(B) =: dst. Return: graded object. Purpose: construct src(A) + src(B) —–> dst given by (A|B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: build R = grobj(module([x,y,z]),intvec(0:3)) and S = grobj(...); def Q = grconcat(R,S); grview(Q); output shows the concatenated graded homomorphism (e.g., r^3 <- r(-1)^2 + r(-2)). Use to form combined source maps into a common destination.

rubrics_metrics.name: grrndmat
rubrics_metrics.description: grrndmat(src,dst[,p,b]), intvec src, dst[, int p, b]. Return: matrix of polynomials. Purpose: generate random matrix compatible with src and dst gradings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: optional arguments p, b are for 'sparsepoly' (by default: 75%, 30000). The procedure is experimental. Example: ring r=32003,(x,y,z),dp; print( grrndmat( intvec(0, 1), intvec(1, 2, 3) ) ); -> prints random polynomial entries compatible with provided gradings.

rubrics_metrics.name: grrndmap
rubrics_metrics.description: grrndmap(S, D), graded objects S and D. Return: graded object. Purpose: construct a random 0-deg graded homomorphism src(S) -> src(D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: build modules D and S, then def H = grrndmap(D,S); grview(H); output: 'Graded homomorphism: r(-1) + r(-2) <- r(-1) + r(-2), given by a square matrix, with degrees...' Demonstrates creating random maps for testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: grrndmap2
rubrics_metrics.description: grrndmap2(D, S), graded objects S and D. Return: graded object. Purpose: construct a random 0-deg graded homomorphism between target of D and S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: build modules D and S, def G = grrndmap2(D,S); grview(G); output shows a graded homomorphism matching the target/source shapes (e.g., r^3 <- r + r(-1) + r), with explicit degree layout printed. Use when random map between target/ source of given graded objects is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: grlifting
rubrics_metrics.description: grlifting(M, N), graded objects M and N. Return: map of chain complexes (as a list). Purpose: construct a map of chain complexes between free resolutions of Img(M) and Img(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: build modules P and D (or grres results), call def G = grlifting(D, P); grview(G); printed output shows chain-map entries (lists of graded homomorphisms) and intermediate traces (e.g., 't: 2' and generator combinations). Example shows use with grres outputs and illustrates typical sizes/degrees. Use to lift maps between images to maps between their resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: grlifting2
rubrics_metrics.description: grlifting2(A, B), graded objects A and B (matrices defining maps). Return: map of chain complexes (as a list). Purpose: construct a map of chain complexes between free resolution of M = coker(A) and N = coker(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: construct presentations PP = grpres(P) and DD = grpres(D) then def T = grlifting2(DD, PP); T; -> T[1]=0, T[2]=... ; shows that grlifting2 returns components of a chain-map and warns with an example that calling grlifting2(P,D) may be WRONG if arguments are in wrong order. Documentation shows how to inspect returned list entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: mappingcone
rubrics_metrics.description: mappingcone(M, N), M, N graded objects. Return: chain complex (as a list). Purpose: construct a free resolution of the cokernel of a random map between Img(M) and Img(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage example: build M = grgens(A), N = grgens(B) from KeneshlouMatrixPresentation outputs, compute R = grlifting(M,N), then def T = mappingcone(M,N); grview(T) produces a graded resolution (r(-1)^10 <-- d_1 -- ...). Further example shows post-processing: U = grtranspose(T[1]); resolution G = mres(U,0); flatten and groebner to form an ideal and compute resolution GI = mres(I,0) and inspect betti numbers. mappingcone is used to combine maps into a resolution of a cokernel and then extract an ideal/resolution for further algebraic checks.
